attacks.claim: CPVC plausibility-band gate [0.30,0.75] is an independent physical second-signal / fail-closed gate over the pigment oil-absorption family, distinct from (adds power beyond) the literature D281 OA-class-band check computed in the same oracle.

closes: Demonstrates the CPVC plausibility-band gate in oil-absorption-cpvc-v1 is not an independent fail-closed second-signal on the real catalog: its own literature-band anomaly (iron_oxide_yellow) passes the CPVC gate undetected, the literature band is a strict subset of the CPVC-accepted OA interval for 7/9 covered pigments, and on average the CPVC gate tolerates 1.6x more multiplicative OA error than the literature band before tripping.
does_not_close: Does NOT claim the Daniel/Asbeck-Van Loo CPVC identity itself is wrong -- the physical relationship and its hard geometric bound (0,1) are untouched.
Does NOT retract the literature OA-class-band check, which is the tighter and more informative of the two gates in the target oracle.
Does NOT modify facts.json, the module manifest, or any signed Phase-0 KPI.
Does NOT alter the target oil-absorption-cpvc-v1 receipt in place -- that artifact is left byte-identical; this is a new, separate audit receipt.
falsification_criterion: If the CPVC plausibility-band gate ([0.30,0.75]) is a genuine independent fail-closed second-signal (not strictly subsumed by the literature-band gate already computed in the same oracle), then for every real catalog OA value the literature-band check itself flags as anomalous, the CPVC gate must ALSO flag it.
headline: CPVC plausibility-band gate [0.30,0.75] signed in oil-absorption-cpvc-v1 is subsumed by (strictly weaker than) the oracle's own literature D281 OA-class-band check for 7/9 covered pigments; the one real catalog anomaly the literature band flags (iron_oxide_yellow, OA=14) is NOT flagged by the CPVC gate (CPVC=0.6254 inside [0.30,0.75]); CPVC gate tolerates 1.6x more multiplicative OA error on average before tripping than the literature band -> the 'independent fail-closed second-signal' framing is refuted on the real catalog, even though checkC's synthetic 10x/0.1x mutation demo (unaffected) still holds.
method: Imported the TARGET receipt's own live oracle module (run_cpvc.py) directly -- reused its LIT_OA_BAND dict, RHO_OIL, CPVC_PLAUS_LO/HI, and cpvc_from_oa() verbatim, no retyped constants -- inverted cpvc_from_oa() to find, per pigment, the full OA interval the CPVC plausibility band would accept, and compared it against the already-published literature band for the same pigment, plus the actual live catalog value.
non_circularity: Consumes only the target's own oracle module + the live facts.json; the OA-interval inversion is an exact algebraic inverse of the target's own cpvc_from_oa(), so it cannot introduce a discrepancy the target's own function would not reproduce forwards.
purpose: Test whether the CPVC plausibility-band gate signed in oil-absorption-cpvc-v1 has independent discriminating power, or is mathematically subsumed by (strictly weaker than) the literature OA-class-band check already computed in the same oracle.

results.named_unflagged_anomaly: pigment.iron_oxide_yellow.oil_abs = 14 g/100g: literature-band-flagged (band [28.0,80.0]) but CPVC = 0.6254 is inside [0.30,0.75] -- NOT flagged
